summary: 20 years later - off to the web! Step one: dragging everything we had into the new world.

changes.text: The editor moved from a Windows .exe to the browser. No install, no gzip.exe, nothing to unpack: open a save, edit, save. Your saves never leave your machine.
English is now the main language, Russian is still here. Switch it any time.
Dark and light themes, both in the spirit of good old Heroes 3. The default theme is "System".
The jokes and wisecracks of the old version moved in too.
Just drop a save onto the window.
Ctrl+O opens a file, Ctrl+S saves it.
Saving goes through the system "Save as" window: the default name gets an se_ prefix, the original stays untouched.
A warning about unsaved edits when you close the tab or open another file.

The editor figures out what wrote the save: Armageddon's Blade (GOG version included), The Shadow of Death, Heroes Chronicles, HD Edition or Horn of the Abyss. For HotA it warns that editing is risky.
HD Edition joins the edition list, still on a test drive.
The edition is picked from the file header, not just from the heroes.
Creature and artifact lists you can search by the first letters.
Level and experience are linked: change the level and the experience follows; with "Level follows the experience" checked it is the other way round.
Spells are laid out like a spell book: levels 1-5 down, Air, Fire, Water and Earth across. Magic Arrow and Visions show up in every school with a four-element badge.
Every spell has a purpose badge: damage, buff, protection, weakening, control, healing, battlefield, special, summoning, adventure. The same badges filter the list.
Hover over a spell and a hint tells its school, level and what it does.

Every artifact in the backpack list has a category badge: attack, defense, power, knowledge, combined, luck and morale, skills, magic, immunity, troops, adventure, resources, special. The same badges filter the list, and a "+" button right in the list puts an artifact into the backpack without closing the list. What the hero already carries is highlighted.
The artifact list shows only what the save's edition knows. The spell book, the spell scroll and the catapult are gone from it altogether: the game glitches with them in the backpack.

Every secondary skill has its own badge, in the list and next to the field. The level shows as stripes: one for basic, two for advanced, three for expert. Skills can now be found by their first letters.

In the army every creature has its town's badge, in the list and next to the field, on the town's colour. The list holds only the creatures the save's edition knows; the hero's own town comes first, level 1 to 7.
The found hero shows the town of their class, and each creature in their army shows its town.
Movement points left today and movement per day: both are editable.
When the editor changes the edition by itself, the edition list in the header winks so you can see what changed.
Fixed old bugs nobody noticed in 20 years (well, almost nobody).
Searching for "Adela" no longer finds "Adelaide".
Saves with a broken gzip checksum (and Heroes writes exactly those) open without complaints.
Half-learned spells in a save no longer get lost when a hero is written back.
Movement points are read and written in full (4 bytes), not as one byte like 2.05 did.
Presets are off to the warehouse for now, but they will be back soon.
